# Reginn and the industries that were always telling its story

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Reginn** works now.

Reginn's dossier runs through the whole Völsung cycle: the otter's ransom in Skáldskaparmál, the fosterage in Reginsmál and Völsunga saga, the reforging of Gram, and the death on Fáfnir's heath when the birds spoke. He is the cycle's great ambiguous figure — the finest smith in the tradition and its coldest traitor, teacher and would-be murderer of the same boy.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Reginn
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Domain of influence:** Dwarf Smith, Fafnir's Brother
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Technology & Innovation · Commerce & Governance · Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Manufacturing, Craft & Automation
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 336 of 437

## The Myth at Work

**The Otter's Ransom.** It begins with a skinned otter.  Óðinn, Hœnir and Loki came to Andvari's falls, where Reginn's brother Ótr fished in otter shape; Loki killed him with a stone, and that evening the gods carried the skin into Hreiðmarr's house and boasted of the catch. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Foster-Father.** The eddic prose introduces him with exact economy: Reginn was Hreiðmarr's son, 'the most skilled of all men, and a dwarf in stature; he was wise, grim, and skilled in magic'.  He came to the court of King Hjálprek in Denmark, where the boy Sigurðr — son of the slain Sigmundr and Hjördís — was being raised, and Reginn became his foster-father. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Manufacturing, Craft & Automation

*Fabrication, industrial craft, and robotics. (Sector: Technology & Innovation)*

*The smith who reforged Gram from Sigmundrs shards — the divine forge that armed the dragon-slayer.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Reginn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Defense, Military & Security

*Defense contracting, security services, and strategic studies. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The sword Gram was his work — the blade that killed Fafnir and then its maker.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Mining & Natural Resources

*Extraction, minerals, and subterranean wealth. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The cursed hoard of Andvari drove his forge; underground wealth shapes the smiths plan.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Reginn performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

## The Long Employment

Reginn's afterlife runs along two tracks.  In the learned tradition he survived as part of the Völsung material — William Morris's Sigurd the Volsung (1876) gives the foster-smith his full cold arc, and Wagner compressed him with Mime into the Nibelung smith of the Ring cycle, where the brother-scheming-for-the-hoard survives almost intact. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity’s documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in manufacturing, craft & automation, defense, military & security, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/reginn/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
